title: Certificates of Deposit: when an automatic renewal falls to be booked after the grace period
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Certificates of Deposit certificate that has matured and is waiting in its grace period. It fixes the moment from which its renewal falls to be booked.

## Rule

The renewal falls to be booked when both of these hold:

1. the certificate's status is still grace period; and
2. more than the tier's grace period length, in calendar days, has passed after the maturity date, counting the day after the maturity date as day 1.

In other words, the renewal falls to be booked from the day after the grace period ends, for as long as the certificate is still shown in grace period status.

## Boundary cases (illustrative grace length of 5 days, not a tier value)

Maturity date 10 June; the last grace day is 15 June (day 5).

| Current date | Days after the maturity date | Status on record | Renewal falls to be booked? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 June | 5 | Grace period | No, exactly the grace length has passed, not more |
| 16 June | 6 | Grace period | Yes |
| 18 June | 8 | Grace period | Yes, the certificate is still waiting in grace status |
| 16 June | 6 | Active | No, the status is no longer grace period |

## Points of judgement

**The grace period ended yesterday, and the certificate still shows grace period status. Is a renewal to be booked?**
Yes. More than the grace length has passed after the maturity date and the status is still grace period.

**Is the day count taken in business days?**
No. Calendar days are counted, starting with the day after the maturity date as day 1.
